description: The plot illustrates how classification accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from about 1 to about 3000, with major ticks shown at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging from 60 to 85 with tick marks every 5 units. The Base series is a dark gray solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 61% at the smallest co-occurrence to about 67% at the largest. FT is a blue solid line with downward triangle markers, rising from about 62% to about 68%. IKE is a red solid line with upward triangle markers, increasing from about 65% to about 70%. MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, rising from about 66% to about 74%. MEMIT is a purple solid line with pentagon markers, increasing from about 66.5% to about 72.5%. ROME is a green solid line with square markers, increasing from about 72% to about 78%, with the last two points appearing nearly flat around 78%.
